body.p: In this amendment, claims 1, 3-10, 12-18, 21, and 22 are pending, with claims 1, 10, and 21 being independent. Claim 21 is amended. Claims 2, 11, 19, and 20 were canceled by prior amendment. Support for these amendments can be found at least in paragraphs 35, 36, and 41, and in FIGS. 1 and 2A of Applicant's disclosure. No new matter has been added.
Applicant appreciates the indication of allowable subject matter in the Office Action. Claims 1, 3-10 and 12-18 are allowed.
Claims 21-22 have been rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 102(a)(2) as being allegedly anticipated by U.S. Publication No. 2021/0150873 to Shouldice et al. (Shouldice).
Amended claim 21 recites, in part:
training a first machine learning model as a student model in a teacher- student architecture to detect a plurality of breathing phases by:
generating labels corresponding to the plurality of breathing phases using a teacher model configured to operate on motion training data
corresponding to human breathing;

teaching the first machine learning model to classify training audio into the plurality of breathing phases based on the labels from the teacher model, wherein the training audio corresponds to the human breathing and
is time aligned with the motion training data;
passively monitoring a user's breathing by detecting audio with an acoustic
sensor of a device; and
classifying breathing of the user into the plurality of breathing phases by
processing solely the audio detected by the acoustic sensor using the first machine
learning model as trained.

Amended claim 21 incorporates certain features of independent claim 1 that were noted in the Allowable Subject Matter section of the Office Action. For example, claim 21 is amended to recite that once the first machine learning model is trained, "classifying breathing of the user into the plurality of breathing phases by processing solely the audio detected by the acoustic sensor using the first machine learning model as trained." Claim 21 also recites features as to how the
first machine learning model is trained using the teacher-student architecture similar to the features of claim 1.
In view of the foregoing, Applicant respectfully submits that claim 21 is allowable.
Accordingly, withdrawal of the 35 U.S.C. § 102(a)(2) rejection of claims 21-22 is respectfully requested.

Reconsideration and a Notice of Allowance are respectfully requested in view of the amended claims and the Remarks presented above. If there are any questions, a telephone call to the undersigned is invited.
Respectfully submitted, /Kevin T. Cuenot/ Date: December 24, 2024
